About

I am a Ph.D. researcher in Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, advised by Prof. Beatriz Lorenzo in the Network Science Lab.

My research asks how network systems can reuse what they have learned when user demand, available resources, and operating conditions change. I work on continual reinforcement learning, cooperative video delivery, semantic content reuse, and resource allocation in edge and UAV-assisted networks.

I combine algorithm design with Python/PyTorch and MATLAB implementation, network simulation, and experimental evaluation. I have been a research assistant in the lab since September 2023. I maintain public research repositories with simulation code, experiment scripts, saved results, and usage documentation.

Selected research

IEEE TMC · 2026 · First author

Continual learning for semantic content reuse

Network decisions must adapt when semantic environments and resource constraints change.

I developed a continual reinforcement learning system that chooses which server serves each user and what content to cache or reuse, subject to latency and resource limits. A shared knowledge base and descriptions of each environment help transfer learned policies when user demand or network conditions change.

Implemented and evaluated in Python/PyTorch with 5 drone-mounted servers, 15 users, and up to 10 environments. The public repository includes training and baseline scripts, saved results, and tools for regenerating experiment figures.

  • Continual reinforcement learning
  • Dictionary learning
  • Python / PyTorch
PaperCode

ImCDN · IEEE VTC-Fall 2026 · Accepted · First author

Cooperative 360° video delivery

Cooperating edge nodes must decide how to deliver and reuse video tiles as network conditions change.

I built a Python simulation that models 360° video as small image regions called tiles, with multiple servers sharing and reusing content. I evaluate how these decisions affect delivery performance as network conditions change.

The conference paper is accepted to IEEE VTC-Fall 2026. An ongoing journal extension studies distributed lifelong learning for cooperative content delivery.

  • Network simulation
  • 360° video
  • Distributed lifelong learning

IEEE Internet of Things Journal · 2025 · First author

Drone positioning and computing task assignment

Mobility, task allocation, and computing resources interact under changing demand and queue congestion.

I implemented a MATLAB framework that chooses drone positions, assigns queued computing tasks to servers, and allocates processing capacity. It combines particle swarm optimization, dynamic programming, and lifelong learning, with separate modules for central training and online network simulation.

  • Constrained optimization
  • Dynamic programming
  • Edge computing
PaperCode

IEEE TWC · 2026 · Co-authored

Lifelong learning for network control

Satellite-terrestrial networks must balance data freshness and energy use across heterogeneous learning domains.

I co-developed learning-based control and resource-allocation methods for satellite and ground networks. A shared knowledge base transfers experience across different network tasks to help balance energy use, data freshness, and adaptation.

The published study reports up to 8 times faster convergence than baseline policy-gradient methods in complex domains.

  • SDN
  • Knowledge transfer
  • Resource allocation

Research code

Explore the implementations behind my published research, with simulation code, saved experiment results, and usage documentation.

Python / PyTorch · IEEE TMC

Adaptive content reuse and continual learning

Learn which server should serve a user and when cached or similar content can replace new computation. The implementation transfers experience between changing network environments through a shared knowledge base.

Includes training scripts, comparisons with baseline learners, saved results, figure-generation tools, and instructions for downloading pretrained lifelong learners.

Explore repositoryExperiment guide

MATLAB · IEEE Internet of Things Journal

Drone positioning, task assignment, and processing allocation

Coordinate a collection drone and 25 drone-mounted servers: choose their positions, assign queued computing tasks, and allocate processing capacity as workloads change.

Includes central training and online simulation modules, baseline comparisons, saved MATLAB results, and a guide connecting paper equations and figures to the code. The repository distinguishes the published experiment version from later model corrections.

Explore repositoryPaper-to-code guide

Python / NumPy / pandas · IEEE UEMCON

Task assignment with application-specific requirements

Model 60 computing tasks and 20 drone-mounted servers, accounting for task type, latency, throughput, and processing resources. Use Q-learning to assign tasks and particle swarm optimization to position servers.

Includes a parameter-sweep command-line entry point, greedy and random baselines, CSV experiment results, and documented simulation settings.

Teaching Assistant

I independently design approximately one-third of the course homework assignments and quizzes, working with professors on course content and assessment.

CS 250 – Introduction To Computation: In the previous semester, I led weekly discussions for a class of approximately 30 students and held one hour of office hours each week. I answered questions and provided patient, individualized guidance through difficult concepts and problems.
